note: Macro risk-intelligence notes + project policy notes for AgentBL's RAG retriever (AI-11). MRI-* notes summarise public data captured on 2026-10-16 (IMF PortWatch transits, Polymarket odds, Yahoo Finance futures, news headlines; see data/real-data/snapshot.json); entries marked illustrative are demo background, not intelligence. Live route evidence for a case comes from src/realdata, not from this file.

documents.text: IMF PortWatch counted about 4 ship transits a day through the Strait of Hormuz in the week to 2026-10-11, against about 70 a year earlier, and merchant ships were attacked and sunk near the strait in mid-October. Polymarket prices under 1% on traffic returning to normal by 31 October and about 11% by 31 December. Cargoes that must transit the strait (Gulf loadings such as Jebel Ali) face indefinite delay; Fujairah loadings bypass it but sit next to it and pay war-risk premiums.

documents.source: Yahoo Finance COMEX HG=F (snapshot 2026-10-16), news headlines
documents.text: Copper trades around USD 14,500/MT (COMEX about USD 6.59/lb on 2026-10-16), close to record levels after mine disruptions and US tariff-driven stockpiling. An unwind of the tariff trade could take prices down quickly, so copper collateral keeps a volatility haircut and is re-marked to the live benchmark rather than the contract price.

documents.source: Yahoo Finance ICE BZ=F and NYMEX HO=F (snapshot 2026-10-16)
documents.text: Brent trades around USD 105/bbl with the Strait of Hormuz largely closed to merchant traffic. Diesel and gasoil cracks are near records, yet ULSD futures fell about 13% over the past month: large swings both ways, so crude- and product-backed collateral needs a volatility haircut.

War-risk cover for Gulf and Gulf of Oman voyages carries additional premiums and short notice of cancellation. Verify that ICC(A) all-risks plus war cover stays valid through the full transit, with a buffer beyond ETA, or the cargo may be under-insured on arrival.

Bab el-Mandeb transits ran about 17% below a year earlier in the week to 2026-10-11, and Suez traffic is near last year's level but still far below pre-2024 volumes. Many Asia-Europe services keep routing round the Cape of Good Hope, which adds 10-14 days to a Shanghai-Hamburg voyage.
Illustrative: Yangshan discharge berth waiting times sit within the normal seasonal range; no material delay risk is priced for copper-cathode discharge at Shanghai.

The oil shock pressures energy-importing Asian currencies. Because buyers pay in USD under the L/C, direct FX exposure to the financing pool is limited; currency weakness is a buyer-side, not pool-side, risk.
Counterparty and vessel screening against the demo sanctions list shows no hits for the demo trade parties; sanction risk is low but must be re-screened if the route or counterparties change.

1 RWA = 1.00 USD is a TARGET redemption value, not a guaranteed repayment. Investor returns come from buying at a discount and from trade repayment; actual redemption depends on importer payment, cargo settlement and insurance coverage. Demo uses permissioned mock investors and does no real fundraising.

Target redemption exposure must stay within the research collateral estimate times the redemption coverage limit (default 0.9). This collateral guardrail caps how much can be issued and acts as a floor on the issue price; the estimate is not independently validated cargo value.

The research RWA discount is the lower of two caps: a share of the exporter's stated or estimated trade profit (faster payout gives up a larger share, and risk adds to it) and an annual-rate ceiling over the financing tenor (FAST 12%, BALANCED 9%, LOW_COST 7% a year, plus 2 points per 100 bps of risk). The issue price is cash / (cash + financing cost); these parameters do not establish an investor risk premium.
